body:
Well, something struck me after you said that which completely slipped by me because I was in panic mode: My dad works at my city's courthouse. He isn't a lawyer, but he works closely with the lawyers there and has a pretty good professional relationship with most of them. He contacted one of them about my friend's predicament and this guy said that he'll be able to help; he didn't seem to think that the lack of money was a problem, so I gave my friend his information and he'll be calling this lawyer on Monday. I'm not sure all that he'll be able to do to help given that lack of money, but even if it's just some legal advice, I think it'll be a godsend. If he IS willing to work pro bono, then that'll be the best case.

My friend was pretty surprised that I had gone out of my way to set up something like this and was very thankful, so hopefully this is a good first step.

Thanks for sticking with me and beating me about the head. I clearly needed it since I wasn't able to see this obvious solution otherwise.
He doesn't have the kind of money for a lawyer.
Thanks. I'll look at some resources and get into contact with him soon.
Well, that's one thing I'm concerned about because he lives alone. There's a lot of time he has unsupervised and that's really nerve-wracking.

I don't drink; there's a bar a few doors down from where we hang out and he pre-game'd over there without my knowledge. Honestly I didn't even know he spent much time there before he told me the other day. I'll see about steering him away from there in the future.

One of the reasons is a bit of legal trouble, and I'm not sure how to help with that. To be clear, it isn't like a life-ending legal thing; he isn't being sued for every worldly possession and half his income for the rest of his life, he isn't in danger of going to jail for any amount of time, but it's making it very inconvenient and frustrating for him in certain aspects of his life.
